panels.title: Consumer Lag by Group
panels.description: kafka_consumergroup_lag_sum from kafka-exporter, summed per consumer group / topic. Watch this during `make chaos-test`'s spark-restart scenario -- lag should climb while spark is down and drain back to ~0 after it recovers.

panels.title: Message Throughput (offset delta, msgs/sec)
panels.description: Substitute for "broker request rate": kafka_exporter (verified against its README) exposes broker count and topic/partition offsets/consumer-group lag, but no broker-native request-rate metric -- that lives in Kafka's own JMX MBeans, which this project deliberately doesn't expose (no JMX agent injected into the apache/kafka image). This approximates throughput from the rate of change of each partition's current offset instead.

panels.title: Spark Structured Streaming Latency (metric name unverified)
panels.description: spark.sql.streaming.metricsEnabled=true (set in docker-compose.yml's spark command) exposes a 'latency' Codahale metric under namespace spark.streaming, component instance=driver -- confirmed against the official Spark 4.1.2 monitoring docs. What is NOT confirmed (no live Spark cluster was available to check): the exact Prometheus metric name PrometheusServlet turns that into, since it depends on the runtime app ID and streaming query name. This panel uses a permissive regex match on job=spark plus '*latency*' in the metric name as a starting point -- open http://spark:4040/metrics/prometheus/ directly (or check Prometheus's own /targets and /graph pages) while the stack is running, find the real metric name, and tighten this query.
